newsitem.title: USA: Compaq launch to ripple through PC industry.
newsitem.headline: Compaq launch to ripple through PC industry.

text.p: Compaq Computer Corp will launch new corporate PCs and a new manufacturing strategy on Thursday that is expected to ripple through the rest of the personal computer industry much in the same manner that its big price cuts in the summer of 1992 changed the PC landscape.

On Thursday, after the world's largest PC maker reports its second quarter earnings, it will hold a press conference in New York to unveil new PCs for corporate users -- its first products to result from its new build-to-order manufacturing. A Compaq spokeswoman in Houston declined to give any details.

Industry analysts said Compaq's widely-anticipated announcements are a response to the success of direct PC maker Dell Computer Corp, which is growing faster than any other PC maker with a lower-cost manufacturing strategy. Dell ships products directly to customers, while Compaq and other PC makers ship to distributors and retailers.

But Compaq will now begin to build-to-order, meaning that it will manufacture PCs as they are ordered by customers, instead of based on market forecasts. Analysts said many of Compaq's distributors and resellers will participate in its manufacturing strategy, which takes costs out of the PC.
"They have taken a lot of costs out of the system," said Louis Mazzucchelli, an analyst with Gerard Klauer & Mattison. "They had a lot of fat to trim out of the old way."

Two of the big costs that Compaq will eliminate with its re-engineering model is a lot of the inventory that sits in the distribution channel. Frequently, this inventory is not in the configurations that customers want, such as PCs with 200 megahertz Pentium processors or more memory.
It will also eliminate some of the costs of its price protection payments for resellers, which Compaq pays resellers when they have to cut prices to move products out the door.

"Without taking some form of action to meet the competition from Dell and to a lesser extent, the other direct vendors like Gateway (2000 Inc ) there would be no stopping Dell," said Eugene Glazer of Fortis Advisers. "Dell is far more efficient, their inventory risk is much lower and they can get new technology to the market faster."

Last April, Compaq's chief financial officer Earl Mason said in an interview that Compaq's re-engineering efforts would lead to PCs that are from 10 to 20 percent lower than Compaq's current prices. Analysts said Compaq's moves will be felt by other PC vendors, especially its pricing.

"With the PC industry slowing and Dell gaining substantial share and other companies that are hurting, they will have to bring their cost structure in line," said Bill Milton, a Brown Brothers Harriman analyst.

Already the NEC Computer Systems unit of Packard Bell NEC Inc announced three weeks ago at PC Expo that it would partially embrace the direct model, by providing direct sales of its commercial systems to their customers if preferred.
Some analysts and industry executives said they expect Compaq to unveil its new corporate PCs at prices either at or lower than prices offered by its fierce Texas rival Dell.
"They are going to be priced very aggressively," Mazzucchelli said. "They are going to meet Dell's pricing."

Already, Hewlett-Packard Co said that it plans to announce next Monday that it will cut prices on commercial PCs, PC workstations and small business PCs, including PCs with PentiumPro and Pentium II chips, by up to 24 percent.
"We are making some significant price reductions on Monday," said a spokesman for H-P's PC business.

Compaq has said in the past that it believes its actions will be as significant to the PC industry as its launch in the summer of 1992 of new lower-cost PCs, which drastically changed the PC industry and fueled an industry-wide price war.

H-P said that its plans for price cuts are not a reaction to Compaq, but have been in the works for several weeks. "They are consistent with our history of pricing leadership, of pricing at or below the industry leaders, of which we are one," the H-P spokesman said.

"We will be competitive," said an International Business Machines Corp PC Co spokesman, when asked about Compaq's expected price cuts. He also said Compaq's build to order plans mirror IBM's advanced assembly program, which has been in place for the past 18 months. "We have been working on manufacturing efficiencies and inventory turns for 18 months," IBM said.
